text:
tara: Heads up — after the cluster upgrades in us-west-2 (rolled 1.30 last night) we're seeing GPU nodegroups not being matched by the autoscaler. Spot pools are spinning up, but CA doesn't attach them to any nodegroup so they never drain/scale-down. Cost alert just fired.

sam: I noticed the same on batch-gpu-prod. Metrics show scale-up requests + nodes provisioning, but CA logs contain repeated `no matching nodegroup for node` messages.

alex: This smells like the providerID/nodeclass field renaming in the nodegroup CRD from the kube-upgrade. CA mapping logic probably still expects the old annotation key.

tara: Logs snippet:```2026-03-17T05:12:03Z cluster-autoscaler: ERROR: no matching nodegroup for node "ip-10-0-123-45.us-west-2.compute.internal" (ProviderID: aws:///us-west-2a/i-0abcdef1234567890) node labels: {kubernetes.io/arch=amd64, beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type=p4d.24xlarge, topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2a}```

kevin: beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type should be deprecated but we still map it. After upgrade the managed nodegroups come with `node.k8s.aws/instanceType` instead (new provider-side annotation). CA doesn't find the nodegroup because it checks `spec.template.metadata.labels` using the old key.

infra-bot: hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/cluster-autoscaler/pulls/487 (adds fallback mapping and tolerates multiple providerID formats) :warning:

sam: Any short-term mitigation? We need to stop the spot burst and avoid more charges.

alex: Temporary workaround we applied to batch-gpu-prod: add the legacy label to Node objects on admission so CA can match. Command we used: `kubectl label nodes -l node.k8s.aws/instanceType=p4d.24xlarge beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type=p4d.24xlarge --overwrite` — not ideal but stops new unmatched nodes.

tara: Also changed CA config: `--scale-down-delay-after-add=20m` -> bumped to 60m to avoid thrash while we patch.

kevin: Is rollback to previous k8s version on the table? That would be heavy.

julia: Not doing rollback. Plan: merge the fallback mapping PR, build quick image, and roll CA tomorrow morning behind a canary. Also we'll add a mutating webhook to populate legacy labels for a few hours during migration — avoids manual node relabeling.

alex: I pushed a small helm values patch to our infra repo (ref: infra/helm/cluster-autoscaler/values.yaml#L98) that enables the feature flag and increases the log level so we can watch.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for cluster-autoscaler (canary: ca-hotfix-487) targeting us-west-2 batch-gpu-prod at 2026-03-17T08:20:00Z

tara: After canary we saw matched nodegroups and two nodes drained cleanly. Will keep monitoring for the next 2 hours before global rollout.

sam: Added a quick dashboard panel to show `count(unmatched_nodes)` and cost burn for spot-gpu pools. If it spikes again we'll pause workloads.

julia: Follow-up items: 1) permanent CA fix to accept both old/new nodeclass/providerID fields (PR 487). 2) add migration playbook to infra runbook for future provider-side label renames. 3) audit other controllers that match node labels.

tara: Thanks everyone — saved a few thousand dollars and avoided a bigger outage. Will post a short postmortem once we finish the rollout. :thumbsup:
